# The Multi-Target Night Planner {#sec-night-planner}

The PLAN tab, in the sidebar right after AUTORUN, is Polaris's
whole-night planner, in the style of ZWO's ASIAIR (a popular
all-in-one imaging controller). Where AUTORUN runs one shooting
schedule against whatever the scope is currently pointed at
(@sec-autorun), PLAN lets you queue several targets in advance, each
with its own frame list, and runs them in order. Between targets it
slews and plate-solve-centers automatically: it takes a short
exposure, matches the stars against a catalog to see exactly where
the scope points, and nudges until the target is centered. Along the
way it can handle guiding (a second camera watching a star so
tracking errors are corrected continuously), cooling, auto-focus, and
the meridian flip (the pier-side swap German equatorial mounts need
when a target crosses the north-south line overhead). When the night
is done, it runs your end-of-session actions.

Under the hood a plan "compiles" to an Advanced Sequencer document and
runs on the same engine as the ADV tab (@sec-adv-sequencer), so only
one of the two can run at a time. PLAN refuses to start while a
sequence is already running, and vice versa, with a clear message in
both directions.

![A target open in the PLAN editor: name and coordinates at the top,
the elevation-tonight chart with draggable green handles setting the
capture window, during-capture automation (re-center, re-focus,

## The plan library

Plans live in a global library in your user profile, not inside a rig,
so a saved plan is runnable with any active rig. A picker row at the
top lets you choose a saved plan or use **New**, **Duplicate**, and
**Delete**. **Export** and **Import** share a plan as a JSON file (a
plain-text data file) so you can load it back on another host.

## Plan settings

Open the plan-settings sheet with the hexagon button to configure the
whole night:

| Setting | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Start** | Begin **now** or **at a clock time**; the runner waits, then starts. |
| **End** | Stop when **all frames are done**, at **astronomical dawn** (when the sun climbs to 18° below the horizon and the sky first begins to brighten), or at a **set time**. |
| **Auto guiding** | Start the active guider (Polaris's built-in one, or PHD2, the free autoguiding program most amateur astrophotographers use) before the first target and stop it at the end. |
| **Auto cooling** | Cool the camera to a target temperature at the start and warm it at the end. |
| **Auto meridian flip** | Flip across the meridian automatically, pausing and resuming the active guider around the flip. |
| **Auto-focus** | Run auto-focus at the start and/or per target. |

### Meridian flip tuning

When auto meridian flip is on, the PLAN panel exposes the flip
parameters directly, so there is no need to visit the AUTORUN or ADV
trigger configuration:

- **Minutes after meridian**: how long past the meridian to wait
  before flipping.
- **Recenter after flip**: plate-solve-center on the target again
  after the flip so framing is preserved.
- **Auto-focus after flip**: run an auto-focus once the flip
  completes.

The flip pauses and resumes whichever guider backend is active, native
or PHD2, not just PHD2 (@sec-guiding).

## Targets

Each plan holds an ordered list of targets, and for every target you
can:

- **Enable or disable** it without removing it from the plan.
- Set its **Name**, **RA/DEC** (right ascension and declination, the
  sky's equivalent of longitude and latitude), **rotation**, and a
  **delay start (min)** that holds the target until it clears an
  obstruction.
- Edit its **per-target frame list**: exposure and count per filter,
  gain, and binning (combining adjacent pixels into one larger, more
  sensitive pixel), edited like the AUTORUN frame rows. A "copy
  frames to all targets" action saves repetitive setup.
- Set **per-target re-center, re-focus, and dither every N frames**
  to keep framing, focus, and dithering maintained within a long
  target run. A dither nudges the mount slightly between frames so
  hot pixels and other fixed-pattern noise land on different sky
  pixels each time.
- **Reorder or delete** it within the list.

### Adding a target

There are four ways to add a target:

- **Catalog search**: find a DSO (deep-sky object: a galaxy, nebula,
  or star cluster) by name or catalog designation from
  the bundled database.
- **Manual RA/DEC**: type coordinates directly.
- **Use current mount position**: capture wherever the scope points
  right now.
- **Frame in the Sky map**: switch to the SKY tab
  (@sec-sky-explorer), frame the target with the FOV (field of view)
  overlay and rotation, then **Add to plan** captures the center
  RA/DEC and the rotation.

## End-of-session actions

When the plan finishes, or reaches its end condition, Polaris can warm
the camera and turn the cooler off, park or home the mount, send the
focuser to zero, and shut down the host. The shutdown action is gated
behind an explicit confirmation, because the device powers off
completely and must be turned back on physically.

## Running a plan

Before you start, **View plan** draws a whole-night timeline graph
with elevation curves per target and per-target delays marked, so you
can sanity-check the order. The Polaris Shutter provides Start and
Stop in the run bar, pinned to the bottom of the panel, alongside
current-target and total progress bars and the target's elevation
during capture. The plan status (waiting for start, running, and the
current target) is mirrored on the HOME dashboard and in the top
status bar, so you can watch the night from any tab.

![The View plan timeline: each target's elevation curve over the
night, its capture window as a colored bar (hatched means waiting for
the window to open), and the summary table with per-target frame
counts, time estimates, and maximum
altitude.](images/plan.jpg){#fig-plan-timeline}

## Notes and current limits

PLAN and ADV share one engine; starting one blocks the other, with a
clear message. Targets are single-frame in this version: mosaic
targets and rotator-driven auto-rotation are planned for a later pass,
so today the **Rotation** field is record-keeping unless you add a
rotator move to the flow yourself.
